industry: Checkomatic — check printing and fulfillment, New York
title: The in-house app that runs Checkomatic
summary: Orders, production, and fulfillment for a national check printer — one custom system that runs the whole operation end to end.
problem: A national check printing business runs on details: every order carries custom artwork, bank data, and print specifications, and a mistake anywhere means reprints and missed ship dates. Off-the-shelf software was never built for that workflow, and the volume had outgrown what manual coordination could handle.
solution: We built and maintain Checkomatic's in-house application. Orders come in from the web store and phone, move through proofing and production queues, and leave with carrier labels and tracking — all in one system the whole team works in. Print specifications, bank validation, and fulfillment rules live in the workflow instead of in people's heads.
result: One system runs the operation end to end. Orders move from placed to printed to shipped without anything retyped, and the owners can see exactly where every order stands at any moment.

title: Porting a shoe company's legacy program to the web
summary: The desktop program the business ran on for years, rebuilt as a modern web application — same workflows, no installs, available anywhere.
problem: The company ran on an aging desktop program that only worked on certain machines, couldn't be used outside the office, and got harder to maintain every year. The business logic inside it — styles, sizes, pricing, orders — was years of accumulated knowledge that existed nowhere else.
solution: We ported the program to a modern web application. The workflows the team already knew stayed the same, the accumulated business rules were preserved and documented as code, and the new system runs in any browser — office, warehouse, or home.
result: The business kept the software it knew, minus the installs and the aging hardware it depended on. Changes that were impossible in the old program are now routine work.

title: A warehouse app that runs receiving to shipping
summary: Inventory, locations, picking, and shipping in one app built around how the warehouse actually works — with barcode scanning throughout.
problem: Inventory lived in a mix of spreadsheets and memory. Receiving wasn't recorded consistently, nobody could say what was on a shelf without walking over to it, and picking mistakes only surfaced after packages had left the building.
solution: We built a warehouse application around the building's real workflow: receiving records stock as it arrives, every item has a location, picking is scanned against the order so errors show up before boxes are sealed, and shipping is generated from what was actually packed.
result: The team can see what's in stock and where it is, mistakes get caught at the scan instead of at the customer, and new warehouse staff are productive in days instead of months.

title: E-commerce rescue and cloud migration
summary: A struggling storefront on shared hosting, migrated to Azure with zero downtime and rebuilt for speed.
problem: Their online store ran on shared hosting that couldn't keep up. Pages were slow, outages were frequent, and there was no room to grow. The platform held years of product data and live customer orders, so any migration had to happen without taking the business offline.
solution: We migrated the entire platform, including a 25GB product database, to Microsoft Azure with a modern setup: dedicated app hosting, managed MySQL, Redis caching, and a global CDN. Then we went after performance directly, lazy-loading third-party scripts, removing duplicate analytics tags, and optimizing the storefront page by page.
result: The migration completed with zero downtime, and page load times dropped dramatically. The store now runs on infrastructure that scales with the business instead of holding it back.

industry: National check printing and fulfillment company
title: Shipping automation for a high-volume printer
summary: FedEx and UPS integrated directly into the order system: live rates, automatic labels, and per-package cost tracking.
problem: Every order meant manual carrier lookups and hand-built shipping labels across FedEx and UPS. At their volume, that was hours of repetitive work each day, and nobody knew what any individual shipment actually cost.
solution: We integrated both carriers' APIs directly into their order system: live negotiated rates with transit times shown at checkout, automatic label generation the moment an order is ready, and per-package cost allocation tied back to every order.
result: Label creation went from a manual step to fully automatic, and shipping costs are now allocated to the penny on every order. The team ships more in less time, with real numbers behind every decision.

title: Finding and removing a hidden email exploit
summary: A malicious injection buried in transactional email templates, found, removed, and locked down.
problem: Something was off with the company's transactional emails. Deliverability was suffering and customers were reporting messages that didn't look right. The templates had been touched by several vendors over the years, and nobody knew what was inside them anymore.
solution: We audited every email template in the system and found a malicious injection hidden in the markup. We removed it, rebuilt the affected templates cleanly, and tightened the sending pipeline, including suppression list management, so the same door couldn't be opened again.
result: Clean templates, restored deliverability, and a documented email pipeline the owner can trust. Sometimes the most valuable work is the problem a client didn't know they had.

industry: Fire protection design firm, New York
title: Automating sprinkler system drafting
summary: A custom AutoCAD plugin that reads floor plans and places sprinkler heads to code automatically.
problem: Sprinkler system drafting meant hours of repetitive AutoCAD work on every project: placing heads room by room and routing pipe, all while keeping every placement compliant with NFPA-13 and NYC building code.
solution: We built a custom AutoCAD plugin that reads the floor plan, extracts rooms automatically from the drawing's own labels, and places sprinkler heads according to code requirements. The engineer reviews and adjusts instead of drafting from scratch.
result: Drafting time per drawing dropped from hours to minutes, and code compliance is built into every placement instead of checked after the fact.
